zh: 欢迎来到 Big Technology Podcast，这是一个关于科技世界及之外冷静、细致对话的节目。

zh: 今天，我们将深入探讨健康，特别是关于 Ozempic 和其他一系列减肥药。

speaker: Unknown
en: Weight loss medicine is starting to make its way into our society and do it fast and change, really change our relationship with food and change our economy effectively.
zh: 减肥药正开始进入我们的社会，而且速度很快，改变了，真正改变了我们与食物的关系，并有效地改变了我们的经济。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to talk about how that's going to happen and then also the pros and cons of these drugs.
zh: 我们将谈论这将如何发生，以及这些药物的利弊。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're joined today by Yohan Hari.
zh: 今天我们邀请到的嘉宾是 Yohan Hari。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's a New York Times bestselling author and his new book, Magic Pill, The Extraordinary Benefits and Disturbing Risks of the New Weight Loss Drugs is out in any bookstore you could hope for.
zh: 他是《纽约时报》畅销书作者，他的新书《Magic Pill: The Extraordinary Benefits and Disturbing Risks of the New Weight Loss Drugs》在你所能想到的任何书店都有售。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've read it.
zh: 我已经读过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a terrific book.
zh: 这是一本很棒的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yohan, welcome to the show.
zh: Yohan，欢迎来到节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, I'm really excited to be with you.
zh: 噢，我很兴奋能和你在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks so much.
zh: 非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're gonna talk a little bit about the effects of the economy, but I really want people to understand sort of what this drug does and what it's up against.
zh: 我们将稍微谈谈对经济的影响，但我真的希望大家理解这种药物的作用以及它面临的是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way that I think we should do that is talking about the Cheesecake Park or the Cheesecake Rats.
zh: 我认为我们应该通过谈论 Cheesecake Park 或 Cheesecake Rats 来做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an example that you have in your book about basically the way that the food industry addicts us to food that's not really good for us.
zh: 这是你书中的一个例子，基本上是关于食品 industry 如何让我们对真正对我们有害的食物上瘾。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's this story about the rats that basically find themselves gorging themselves on cheesecake and can't stop that.
zh: 有一个关于老鼠的故事，基本上发现自己在狼吞虎咽地吃芝士蛋糕并且无法停止。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, my wife and I have now started to take in, we've started to, when we're eating dessert nonstop, we just look at each other and we're like, oh no, cheesecake rat.
zh: 你知道，我妻子和我现在已经开始，当我们不停吃甜点时，我们只是看着对方，然后说，噢不，芝士蛋糕老鼠。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what is the cheesecake rat in the Cheesecake Park?
zh: 那么 Cheesecake Park 里的芝士蛋糕老鼠到底是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we're in this incredible position.
zh: 嗯，我们处于这种难以置信的地位。

speaker: Unknown
en: 47% of Americans want to take these new weight loss drugs because they produce an incredible amount of weight loss that I'm sure we're going to unpack.
zh: 47% 的美国人想要服用这些新的减肥药物，因为它们产生了令人难以置信的减肥效果，我相信我们将会拆解这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in a way, when you first hear that, it seems like a kind of mind-blowing moment.
zh: 在某种程度上，当你第一次听到这个时，这似乎是一个令人兴奋的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first time in human history that almost half of us would want to take a drug in order to stop ourselves from eating, right?
zh: 人类历史上第一次，几乎有一半人会想要服用一种药物来阻止自己进食，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you think, well, how did we get here?
zh: 所以你会想，嗯，我们是怎么走到这一步的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What happened to us?
zh: 我们发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, understanding how we got here is very important to understanding the later question of how these drugs work.
zh: 实际上，理解我们如何走到这一步对于理解后面关于这些药物如何起作用的问题非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I guess the way I would get into explaining the experiment you're alluding to is I would say to everyone, just stop for a moment, pause this podcast,
zh: 我想我可以进入解释你提到的实验的方式，我会对大家说，稍等一下，暂停这个播客，

speaker: Unknown
en: And Google something for me.
zh: 并帮我 Google 一样东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Google photographs of beaches in the United States in the year I was born, 1979, and just look at them for a minute and then come back.
zh: Google 搜索我出生那年即 1979 年美国海滩的照片，看它们一分钟，然后再回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you will have noticed about those beaches something that seems really strange to us.
zh: 所以你会注意到关于那些海滩的一些对我们来说似乎真的很奇怪的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone in those pictures pretty much looks to us like what we would call skinny, right, or jacked.
zh: 那些照片里的每个人对我们来说看起来都很像我们所说的瘦，对吧，或者结实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you look at it and go, well, huh, where was everyone else on the beach that day in 1979?
zh: 你看着它然后想，嗯，哈，1979年那天海滩上的其他人都在哪儿呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: But it turns out that's just what Americans looked like in 1979, right?
zh: 但事实证明，那只是1979年美国人的样子，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Obesity was extremely low in the year I was born, and it has exploded in my lifetime.
zh: 在我出生的那一年，肥胖率极低，而在我的一生中它爆炸式增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Between the year I was born and the year I turned 21, obesity doubled in the United States, and then in the next 20 years, severe obesity doubled again.
zh: 在我出生的那一年到我21岁那一年之间，美国的肥胖率翻了一番，然后在接下来的20年里，重度肥胖又翻了一番。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're in this bizarre situation.
zh: 所以我们处于这种奇怪的境地。

speaker: Unknown
en: Human beings exist for about 300,000 years and obesity is very rare.
zh: 人类存在了大约30万年，而肥胖一直很罕见。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then from looking at you, I'm guessing you're pretty similar age to me.
zh: 然后看着你，我猜你的年龄和我差不多。

speaker: Unknown
en: In our lifetimes, obesity exploded.
zh: 在我们的一生中，肥胖爆发了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why?
zh: 为什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What happened?
zh: 发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We know the answer, the most important part of the answer.
zh: 我们知道答案，这是答案中最重要的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obesity explodes everywhere that makes one change.
zh: 肥胖在所有做出一个改变的地方都会爆发。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not where people suddenly lack willpower or become lazy.
zh: 这不是人们突然缺乏意志力或变得懒惰的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's where people move from mostly eating a diet based on whole, fresh foods that they prepare on the day they eat them,
zh: 这是人们从主要吃当天食用的、由新鲜全食构成的饮食，

speaker: Unknown
en: ...to mostly eating a diet of processed and ultra-processed foods which are constructed out of chemicals in factories in a process that isn't even known as cooking, it's called manufacturing food.
zh: ……转变为主要吃由工厂里的化学物质构建而成的加工食品和超加工食品，这个过程甚至不被称为烹饪，它被称为制造食品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns out this new kind of food that's built out of chemicals affects us in a completely different way to the whole fresh foods that human beings ate the 300,000 years before that.
zh: 事实证明，这种由化学物质构建的新型食物对我们的影响，与人类在此之前30万年里吃的全食完全不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the ways it affects us, one of the most important ways, is processed and ultra-processed food undermines our ability to ever feel full, our ability to ever feel we've had enough and then want to stop eating.
zh: 它影响我们的方式之一，也是最重要的方式之一，是加工食品和超加工食品破坏了我们感到饱足的能力，让我们永远无法感到已经足够并想要停止进食。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I go through loads of evidence for this in my book, and there are many different ways in which processed food has this effect on us.
zh: 我在我的书中为此列举了大量证据，加工食品通过许多不同的方式对我们产生这种影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you allude to an experiment that, to me, just totally nailed the effect.
zh: 但你提到的一个实验，在我看来，完全证实了这种影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: I nicknamed it Cheesecake Park.
zh: 我把它昵称为芝士蛋糕乐园。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not the official title.
zh: 这不是官方标题。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is an experiment that was done by a brilliant scientist named Dr. Paul Kenney, who's the head of neuroscience at Mount Sinai in New York.
zh: 这是一个由一位名叫 Paul Kenney 博士的杰出科学家所做的实验，他是纽约西奈山神经科学系的负责人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Dr. Kenney grew up in Dublin in Ireland, and he moved to the United States in the 90s to San Diego to continue his scientific research, to do his PhD, in fact.
zh: Kenney 博士在爱尔兰都柏林长大，他在90年代搬到美国圣地亚哥继续他的科学研究，实际上是去攻读他的博士学位。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he quickly noticed, huh, Americans don't eat like Irish people did at the time, right?
zh: 他很快注意到，哈，美国人的饮食习惯不像当时的爱尔兰人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: They ate, Americans at the time ate much more, and now obviously, ate much more processed and ultra-processed foods.
zh: 他们吃，当时的美国人吃得更多，而且显然，吃了更多的加工食品和超加工食品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like many a good immigrant, Dr. Kenny assimilated and quite quickly became, you know, gained a huge amount of weight.
zh: 像许多优秀的移民一样，Kenney 博士同化了，并且相当快地变得，你知道，增加了大量的体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: He gained 30 pounds in a year or two.
zh: 他在一两年内增加了30磅。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he started to feel like this food he was eating wasn't just affecting his gut, it was affecting his brain, it was affecting how he felt and what he wanted.
zh: 他开始感觉到他吃的这种食物不仅仅影响他的肠胃，它影响他的大脑，影响他的感觉和他的欲望。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he designed this experiment to test it.
zh: 所以他设计了这个实验来测试它。

speaker: Unknown
en: He raised a load of rats in a cage.
zh: 他在笼子里养了一群老鼠。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all they had to eat was the kind of natural whole foods that rats evolved to eat over thousands of years.
zh: 它们唯一能吃的就是那种老鼠在数千年里进化出来的天然全食。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when that's all they had, the rats would eat when they were hungry and then they would stop when they were full.
zh: 当只有这些东西吃的时候，老鼠会在饿的时候吃，然后在饱的时候停止。

speaker: Unknown
en: They had some kind of natural nutritional wisdom that said, hey guys, you've had enough now.
zh: 它们有某种天然的营养智慧，说，嘿伙计们，你们现在吃得够多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They never became overweight.
zh: 它们从未超重。

speaker: Unknown
en: They never became obese.
zh: 它们从未变得肥胖。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then Professor Kenny introduced them to the American diet, the stuff I've been eating all my life too.
zh: 然后 Kenny 教授向它们介绍了美国饮食，我这一辈子也一直在吃的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: He fried up some bacon.
zh: 他煎了一些培根。

speaker: Unknown
en: He bought some Snickers bars.
zh: 他买了一些士力架棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Crucially, he bought a load of cheesecake.
zh: 关键是，他买了很多芝士蛋糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he put it down alongside the healthy food.
zh: 他把它和健康食物一起放下。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the rats went apeshit for the American diet.
zh: 老鼠们对美国饮食发疯了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if rats can go apeshit, if that's a mixed medical.
zh: 我不知道老鼠能不能发疯，如果那是混合医学术语的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: The rats went crazy for the American diet.
zh: 老鼠们对美国饮食疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They would dive into the cheesecake and eat their way out and emerge just completely slicked with cheesecake.
zh: 它们会冲进芝士蛋糕，一路吃过去，然后出来时完全沾满了芝士蛋糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: They ate and ate.
zh: 它们吃啊吃。

speaker: Unknown
en: And eight and eight.
zh: 吃个不停。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way Dr. Kenny put it to me was within a couple of days they were different animals.
zh: Kenny 博士对我描述的方式是，在几天之内它们就变成了不同的动物。

speaker: Unknown
en: That kind of natural nutritional wisdom that they'd had when they had the kind of food they evolved for vanished and they all became severely obese.
zh: 当它们有那种进化来的食物时，它们拥有的那种天然营养智慧消失了，它们都变得严重肥胖。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then Professor Kenny tweaked the experiment again.
zh: 然后 Kenny 教授再次调整了实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: He took away all the American food in a way that feels to me pretty cruel as a former KFC addict, and he left them with nothing but the healthy food they'd evolved to eat that they'd had when they were growing up.
zh: 他拿走了所有的美式食物，在某种程度上，作为肯德基（KFC）上瘾者，我觉得这相当残酷，他留给他们的只有他们进化中习惯吃的健康食物，那是他们成长过程中所拥有的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he was pretty sure he knew what would happen.
zh: 而且他非常确信他知道会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: He thought they would eat more of the healthy food than they had before, and this would prove that exposure to junk food expands the number of calories you eat in a day.
zh: 他认为他们会比以前吃更多的健康食物，这将证明接触垃圾食品会扩大你一天中摄入的卡路里数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is not what happened.
zh: 但那并不是发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something much weirder happened.
zh: 发生了更奇怪的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once they'd had the American diet and it was taken away, they refused to eat the healthy food at all.
zh: 一旦他们有了美式饮食，然后它被拿走了，他们就完全拒绝吃健康食物。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like they no longer recognized it as food.
zh: 就好像他们不再把它当作食物了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They would rather starve than eat that food.
zh: 他们宁愿挨饿也不吃那种食物。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was only when they were literally wasting away that they finally went back to eat it.
zh: 只有当他们真的在消瘦枯萎时，他们才终于回去吃它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I would argue we are all living in a version of Cheesecake Park now.
zh: 现在，我想说我们都生活在芝士蛋糕公园的一个版本里。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are living in an environment from when we're very young where we're fed foods that physically change us and undermine our ability to ever feel full and know when to stop eating.
zh: 我们生活在一个环境中，从我们很小的时候起，我们就被喂食那些在生理上改变我们的食物，这破坏了我们感觉饱的能力，并知道何时停止进食。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not the only thing going on, but it's the key reason why we have this huge obesity crisis and why there is such enormous demand for these new weight loss drugs.
zh: 这并不是唯一发生的事情，但这是我们有这个巨大的肥胖危机的关键原因，也是为什么对这些新的减肥药物有如此巨大的需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like whenever I'm just like about to finish a pack of cookies in one sitting, I'm just like, oh yeah, here I am.
zh: 每当我正要一口气吃完一整包饼干时，我就觉得，哦是的，我就在这儿了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cheesecake rat.
zh: 芝士蛋糕老鼠。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious how they've been able to engineer the food.
zh: 我很好奇他们是如何设计食物的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, obviously we're going to talk about Ozempic as an answer to this, but before we get into that, how have they been able to engineer the food to make us never feel full?
zh: 我的意思是，显然我们要谈论 Ozempic 作为对此的答案，但在我们讨论那个之前，他们是如何设计食物让我们从不觉得饱的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it intentional or is it just a byproduct of the type of food that exists when it's manufactured, as you mentioned, versus whole foods?
zh: 这是故意的，还是仅仅因为当食物被制造时，正如你提到的那样，与全食物相比，现有食物类型产生的副产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the honest answer to your question is a bit complicated.
zh: 我认为对你的问题的诚实回答有点复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's definitely not happening is they're not like James Bond villains going, how can we make everyone as obese as possible?
zh: 绝对没有发生的是，他们不像詹姆斯·邦德（James Bond）电影里的反派那样，想着我们要如何让尽可能多的人肥胖？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not happening, right?
zh: 这并没有发生，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That would be a stupid way of thinking about it.
zh: 那将是一种愚蠢的思考方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's in some ways much more simple.
zh: 在某种程度上，这要简单得多。

en: If you're the head of a KFC, Kraft, any of the food companies, you have a fiduciary responsibility to your shareholders to maximize profit.

zh: 现在，每个认识 Jeff 的人看着他都会说，哇，Jeff 怎么了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: He looks completely different.
zh: 他看起来完全不一样了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the reasons there's these shortages is that everyone then becomes a walking ad.
zh: 所以出现短缺的原因之一是每个人都变成了活广告。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so demand produces demand, produces demand, produces demand in this cascading effect.
zh: 所以需求产生需求，产生需求，产生需求，产生这种级联效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: So although they have been, Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly, the companies that make these drugs, have been massively, to be fair to them, expanding production.
zh: 尽管他们一直在，诺和诺德和礼来，生产这些药物的公司，一直在大规模地，公平地说，扩大生产。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, they want to, they want to make the money.
zh: 当然，他们想，他们想赚钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're racing to get to a finishing line that's just getting further and further away because the more they race, the more people want it, right?
zh: 他们正在赛跑奔向终点线，但这终点线却越来越远，因为他们越是赛跑，人们就越是想要，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So lots of companies are producing compounded copies of these drugs.
zh: 所以很多公司都在生产这些药物的配制仿制品。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's inherently risks in that.
zh: 这本身就有风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not made in FDA labs.
zh: 它们不是在 FDA 实验室生产的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In Austria recently, there was a big problem where people bought what they thought was compounded semaglutides, the active component of these drugs.
zh: 最近在奥地利，发生了一个大问题，人们购买了他们认为是配制的 semaglutides，即这些药物的有效成分。

speaker: Unknown
en: They weren't.
zh: 但它们不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: They went into comas.
zh: 他们陷入了昏迷。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were horribly injured.
zh: 他们受了重伤。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's an inherent risk in compounded versions for obvious reasons.
zh: 出于显而易见的原因，配制版本存在固有风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I understand why people are doing it, right?
zh: 但我理解人们为什么要这样做，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, there's a tremendous complexity.
zh: 所以是的，这极其复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you're right that big pharma will be pressuring to close those loopholes pretty soon.
zh: 我认为你是对的，大型制药公司将很快施压关闭这些漏洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, they're already sending out lawyers letters to health spas.
zh: 我的意思是，他们已经在向健康水疗中心发送律师函了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that happens, I mean, you could abruptly have people thrown off the medicine, whereas like they can afford the compounded drug, they cannot afford 1300 a month.
zh: 如果发生这种情况，我的意思是，人们可能会突然被迫断药，而他们还买得起配制的药物，却负担不起每月 1300 美元的费用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what happens if you get abruptly tossed off the drug?
zh: 那么如果你突然被停药会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's a really important question.
zh: 嗯，这是一个非常重要的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to explain what the drug companies say, and I want to explain why they're probably right, but we need to take it with a small pinch of salt.
zh: 所以我想解释一下制药公司的说法，我想解释一下为什么他们可能是对的，但我们需要对此稍微打个折扣。

speaker: Unknown
en: What the drug companies say is these drugs are like statins or blood pressure meds.
zh: 制药公司的说法是，这些药物就像他汀类药物或降压药。

speaker: Unknown
en: They work for as long as you take them, and when you stop taking them, they stop working.
zh: 只要你服用它们，它们就起作用，当你停止服用时，它们就停止工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you regain the weight pretty rapidly.
zh: 所以你会相当迅速地恢复体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they have funded a study that seems to demonstrate this.
zh: 他们资助的一项研究似乎证明了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The vast majority of people regain the vast majority of their weight within a year.
zh: 绝大多数人在一年内恢复了绝大多数的体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a small pinch of salt in that, in that of course they have a vested interest in telling us that we have to take them forever because they make money forever.
zh: 对此需要稍微打个折扣，因为当然，他们有既得利益告诉我们必须永远服用这些药，因为他们可以永远赚钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: There do seem anecdotally to be some people who take them for a shorter period, use them to radically change their habits, and then seem to stay at a lower weight, although I suspect they're a minority.
zh: 从轶事来看，确实似乎有一些人服用的时间较短，利用它们来彻底改变他们的习惯，然后似乎保持在较低的体重，尽管我怀疑他们是少数。

speaker: Unknown
en: There'll be more research on this soon.
zh: 很快会有更多关于这方面的研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, if you're thrown off, you'll almost certainly regain the weight.
zh: 但是是的，如果你被停药，你几乎肯定 will 恢复体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right, and that could be a very big issue as we see again these opposing forces sort of try to jockey for position here as this drug takes off.
zh: 好的，这可能是一个非常大的问题，正如我们再次看到这些对立势力试图在这个药物起飞时争夺位置一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be worse than that.
zh: 情况可能比那更糟。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know, and there's a lot of things we don't know about these drugs.
zh: 我们不知道，而且关于这些药物有很多我们不知道的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is, so we know if you gained a load of weight now and then went on a diet and lost weight, just through calorie restriction and exercise, so not using these drugs,
zh: 其中一个是，所以我们知道如果你现在增加了很多体重然后节食减肥，仅仅通过热量限制和锻炼，所以不使用这些药物，

speaker: Unknown
en: We know that slows down your metabolism over time.
zh: 我们知道那会随着时间的推移减慢你的新陈代谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes it harder to keep weight off, right?
zh: 这让保持体重变得更难，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you yo-yo diet, if you gain weight, lose weight, gain weight, lose weight, it can really wreck your metabolism so you actually burn calories very slowly.
zh: 如果你反复节食减肥，如果你增重、减重、增重、减重，这真的会破坏你的新陈代谢，所以你实际上燃烧卡路里的速度非常慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know if taking these drugs and then coming off them slows down your metabolism.
zh: 我们不知道服用这些药物然后停药是否会减慢你的新陈代谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably does.
zh: 很可能会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most other forms of weight loss do.
zh: 大多数其他形式的减肥都会。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, all other forms of weight loss do.
zh: 事实上，所有其他形式的减肥都会。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's another concern as well.
zh: 所以这也是另一个担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could you actually end up fatter than you were if you hadn't taken the drug?
zh: 如果你没有服用这种药，你最终会不会反而比以前更胖？

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know, but it's a concern.
zh: 我们不知道，但这是一个担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things that I found so interesting in your book was this concept of a set point that your body basically figures out the weight that you are, the weight that you should be.
zh: 我在你的书中发现的最有趣的事情之一就是设定点的概念，你的身体基本上会弄清楚你的体重，你应该有的体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you try to move too far off of it, at least in terms of the negative, it will try to bring you back up to that set point of weight.
zh: 如果你试图偏离它太远，至少在负面方面，它会试图让你回升到那个体重设定点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, this is really interesting because there's the way people used to think about this in the 60s and 70s and there's the way we understand it now.
zh: 嗯，这真的很有趣，因为人们在 60 和 70 年代思考这个问题的方式和我们现在的理解方式之间存在差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in the 60s and 70s, scientists thought that your weight was basically set from birth or even in utero, that basically from when you're born, you have a certain fat percentage that's kind of innate to you, right?
zh: 所以在 60 和 70 年代，科学家认为你的体重基本上是从出生时甚至在子宫内就设定好的，基本上从你出生开始，你就有一个内在的脂肪百分比，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So think about your temperature set point as an analogy.
zh: 所以把你的温度设定点作为一个类比来思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a natural set body temperature.
zh: 我们有一个天然的设定体温。

speaker: Unknown
en: if you go higher than that your body works very hard to bring it down it makes you sweat it makes you really want to get into the shade if you go lower than that your body works really hard to bring it up it makes you shiver it makes you seek warmth and it was thought that so it's very hard to stay out you basically you can't stay outside your safe temperature level your temperature set point for very long right your body really works to keep you there and if you do stay on it for long you get very unwell
zh: 如果你高于那个，你的身体会非常努力地把它降下来，它让你出汗，它让你真的很想躲到阴凉处，如果你低于那个，你的身体会非常努力地把它升上去，它让你发抖，它让你寻找温暖，人们认为所以很难待在外面你基本上你不能待在你的安全温度水平之外你的温度设定点很长时间对吧你的身体真的努力让你待在那里如果你确实待在那里很长时间你会很不舒服

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was thought that there was something similar with your weight, that you had an innate set point that just sort of regulated.
zh: 所以人们认为体重也有类似的情况，你有一个内在的设定点，只是某种程度上的调节。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could go a little bit above or a little bit below, but it was basically set and regulated.
zh: 你可以稍微高一点或稍微低一点，但它基本上是设定和调节的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the obesity crisis happened, mainly starting in the early 1980s, late 70s, early 80s when I was born.
zh: 然后肥胖危机发生了，主要从 1980 年代早期，70 年代后期，80 年代早期开始，也就是我出生的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not blaming myself.
zh: 我不是在责怪我自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not like Damien in The Omen, couldn't cause it.
zh: 我不像《凶兆》里的 Damien，我不可能是起因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that seemed to blow setpoint theory up, right?
zh: 这似乎推翻了设定点理论，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, what's going on?
zh: 那么，这是怎么回事？

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's set, if it's innate and biological,
zh: 如果它是设定的，如果它是内在的和生物性的，

speaker: Unknown
en: How come it changed so much so quickly?
zh: 怎么会这么快发生了这么大的变化？

speaker: Unknown
en: But what scientists realized, this is contested, but I think it's quite persuasive, is actually what happens is you do have an innate set point, but as you gain weight, your set point rises.
zh: 但是科学家意识到的，这有争议，但我认为它很有说服力，实际上发生的是你确实有一个内在的设定点，但是随着你体重的增加，你的设定点也会上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is really important for understanding why the alternative to these drugs, diet and exercise, does not produce sustained weight loss for about 85% of people who try it.
zh: 这对于理解为什么这些药物的替代方案，饮食和运动，对于尝试它的人中大约 85% 的人不能产生持续的减肥效果非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's say that you now gained 40 pounds.
zh: 假设你现在增加了 40 磅。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you try to lose that 40 pounds through calorie restriction and exercise.
zh: 你试图通过限制卡路里和运动来减掉那 40 磅。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because your innate set point has risen, your brain is trying to hold you at that higher weight.
zh: 因为你的内在设定点已经上升，你的大脑试图让你保持在那个较高的体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: All sorts of physical and biological changes will happen in your brain and your body to try to stop you going down.
zh: 你的大脑和身体中会发生各种身体和生物变化，试图阻止你下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will slow your metabolism down so you burn calories more slowly.
zh: 它会减慢你的新陈代谢，这样你燃烧卡路里的速度会更慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will make you crave more sugary, salty foods.
zh: 它会让你渴望更多含糖、咸的食物。

speaker: Unknown
en: All sorts of changes happen.
zh: 各种各样的变化都会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's lots of evidence for that, overwhelming evidence about metabolic slowdown, for example.
zh: 对此有很多证据，关于新陈代谢减慢的压倒性证据，例如。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember when I first learned that, thinking, well, that can't be true.
zh: 我记得当我第一次了解到这一点时，我想，嗯，那不可能是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because why, obesity is really bad for your health.
zh: 因为为什么，肥胖对你的健康真的非常有害。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would evolution endow us with the desire to hold onto, or biological mechanisms to hold onto obesity, given that obesity is so bad for us?
zh: 考虑到肥胖对我们如此有害，为什么进化会赋予我们保持肥胖的愿望，或者保持肥胖的生物机制？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so maladaptive.
zh: 它是非常不适应的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't make sense to me.
zh: 这对我来说说不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was explained to me by Professor Michael Lowe, who I mentioned before at Drexel.
zh: 德雷塞尔大学（Drexel）的 Michael Lowe 教授向我解释了这一点，我之前提到过他。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best way of thinking about this, I think, which is you've got to think about the circumstances where human beings evolved.
zh: 我认为思考这个问题的最好方式是，你必须考虑人类进化的环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the circumstances where human beings evolved,
zh: 在人类进化的环境中，

speaker: Unknown
en: The situation we live in now essentially never happened or vanishingly rarely, which is where you have...
zh: 我们现在生活的处境基本上从未发生过或极其罕见，也就是你有……

speaker: Unknown
en: Infinite, abundant calories all around you, far more than you could consume, and they last your whole life, right?
zh: 无限的、丰富的卡路里在你周围，远远超过你能消耗的，而且它们持续你的一生，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That just never happened.
zh: 那从未发生过。

speaker: Unknown
en: So evolution did not prepare us for that scenario.
zh: 所以进化没有让我们为那种情况做好准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: The scenario that did happen quite frequently that evolution did prepare us for is the exact opposite, famine.
zh: 进化确实让我们做好准备的那个相当频繁发生的情况恰恰相反，饥荒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Famine was very common, right?
zh: 饥荒很常见，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: In the circumstances where human beings evolved, it was quite likely there would be a famine in your lifetime.
zh: 在人类进化的环境中，你的一生中很有可能发生饥荒。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about it in that context, it makes perfect sense that if you gain weight, your body fights to hold on to the weight, right?
zh: 如果你在这个背景下思考，如果你增重，你的身体会努力保持体重，这完全讲得通，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: If there's a famine, the fattest man at the start is the last man standing, right?
zh: 如果发生饥荒，开始时最胖的人是最后站着的人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a famine.
zh: 发生过一场饥荒。

speaker: Unknown
en: The version of me from three years ago is going to still be alive at the end, whereas Timothee Chalamet will die in week one, right?
zh: 三年前的那个我最后还会活着，而 Timothee Chalamet 会在第一周死掉，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll cry over his body, but he'll bury him and we'll have to move on, right?
zh: 我会对着他的尸体哭泣，但他会埋葬他，我们得继续前进，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Rest in peace.
zh: 安息吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 确实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rest in peace, Timothee Chalamet.
zh: 安息吧，Timothee Chalamet。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 确实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Big Tim.
zh: Big Tim。

speaker: Unknown
en: This innate set point is preparing us for a famine that now is never going to come, right?
zh: 这种内在的定值正在为我们一场现在永远不会到来的饥荒做准备，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So that explains why diets don't work.
zh: 所以这解释了为什么节食不起作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also explains one theory, although this is significantly more contentious.
zh: 它也解释了一个理论，尽管这要更有争议得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a huge debate about what these drugs...
zh: 关于这些药物在做什么存在巨大的争论……

speaker: Unknown
en: So we now know these drugs are primarily working not on your gut, but on your brain.
zh: 所以我们现在知道这些药物主要不是作用于你的肠道，而是你的大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have GLP-1 receptors, not just in your gut, but in your brain.
zh: 你的肠道和大脑里都有 GLP-1 受体。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're profoundly changing our brains.
zh: 它们正在深刻地改变我们的大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: From interviewing the cutting edge neuroscientists, as I did for my book, this is very clear.
zh: 从采访那些前沿的神经科学家来看，正如我为我的书所做的那样，这是很清楚的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's so disconcerting to interview the leading neuroscientists and you say to them, well, what is it doing to my brain?
zh: 采访顶尖的神经科学家是非常令人不安的，你对他们说，嗯，它对我的大脑在做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they kind of go, yeah, come back and ask us in a few years, we don't really know.
zh: 他们有点像，是啊，过几年再来问我们，我们真的不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: But one theory about what it may be doing to the brain is it may be lowering your biological set point.
zh: 但关于它可能对大脑做什么的一个理论是，它可能正在降低你的生物学定值。

speaker: Unknown
en: The equivalent of, this is a very crude analogy, I suspect the scientists I interviewed would think it was overly crude, but it's a bit like taking your set point, resetting your iPhone to the factory settings, right?
zh: 这相当于，这是一个非常粗略的类比，我怀疑我采访的科学家会认为这过于粗略，但这有点像拿你的定值，把你的 iPhone 重置为出厂设置，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It lowers your set point for the duration that you take the drugs.
zh: 在你服用药物的持续时间内，它降低了你的定值。

speaker: Unknown
en: So again, you see, the debate about what causes obesity is intimately related to the debate about how these drugs work in all sorts of fascinating ways.
zh: 所以同样，你看，关于肥胖成因的辩论与关于这些药物如何起效的辩论密切相关，以各种迷人的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you mentioned brain chemistry.
zh: 你提到了脑化学。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's something that I definitely want to talk about.
zh: 这绝对是我想要谈论的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just want to talk about whether kids should be taking these drugs.
zh: 我只是想谈谈孩子们是否应该服用这些药物。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the kids, the US at least, has approved kids as young as 12 taking these drugs.
zh: 我认为孩子们，至少在美国，已经批准了低至 12 岁的孩子服用这些药物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're going to do that on the other side of this break, back right after this.
zh: 我们将在这次休息的另一边进行讨论，这个广告之后马上回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today's executives are more threatened, more exposed, and more vulnerable than ever before.
zh: 如今的高管比以往任何时候都受到更多的威胁，暴露得更多，也更脆弱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Corporations spend billions on workplace security.
zh: 公司在职场安全上花费数十亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what happens when a threat finds your executives outside the office?
zh: 但是当威胁在办公室之外找到你的高管时会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: 70% of attacks on executives happen at home or away from the office.
zh: 针对 70% 的高管攻击发生在家中或远离办公室的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Ironwall understands a terrifying reality.
zh: Ironwall 了解一个可怕的现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: If someone has a grievance against your company, the first place they turn to is Google.
zh: 如果有人对你的公司有不满，他们首先求助的是 Google。

speaker: Unknown
en: It takes them about five minutes to find one of your executives' home addresses online.
zh: 他们大约需要五分钟就能在网上找到你的一位高管的家庭住址。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if their personal information is sitting on the open web, they're far too easy to find.
zh: 如果他们的个人信息在开放网络上，他们就太容易被找到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The team at Ironwall knows this better than anyone.
zh: Ironwall 的团队比任何人都更清楚这一点。
